helpText:
HelpThis ScreenIP Exclusions
Manage IP addresses excluded from all analytics data, and configure date-based data filtering.

Why Exclude IPs?
When you or your team visit the site, those visits show up in analytics and skew the data. Excluding your IP addresses ensures you only see real visitor activity.

Date Filter
At the top, you can enable a date filter to exclude all data before a specified date. This applies to MEMOPYK logs only (not GA4). Toggle Enable Date Filter to turn it on, then pick a start date. Useful for filtering out pre-launch test traffic.

IP Exclusion List
Below the date filter, the "IP Exclusions" section shows all excluded IPs in a table with columns: Label + IP/CIDR, User Agent, Status, Created, and Actions.

Buttons above the table:

  Show IP — Reveals your current IP address (partially masked by default for privacy).
  Exclude My IP — Detects your current IP address and adds it to the exclusion list with one click.
  Add Exclusion — Manually enter an IP address or range. You can add an optional label (e.g., "Stéphane home", "Office") to remember why it was excluded.


Per-row controls:

  Toggle switch — Enable or disable an exclusion without deleting it. Useful for temporary changes.
  Delete button (trash icon) — Permanently remove an exclusion entry.


IP Ranges
You can exclude entire networks using CIDR notation (e.g., 192.168.1.0/24 excludes all 256 addresses in that range). This is useful for office networks where many devices share a range.

Header Badge
The IPs: N badge in the analytics header shows how many IPs are currently excluded. This badge appears on all analytics tabs so you always know exclusions are active.

Tips

  Add all team members' IPs to get clean visitor data — your visits shouldn't count as real traffic
  Labels help you remember why an IP was excluded months later

  AI Context — Brand Brain for Claude

  The AI Context (Brand Brain) defines how Claude writes for MEMOPYK. Every AI-generated blog post, translation, and content piece uses these guidelines automatically. Think of it as training Claude to write in MEMOPYK's voice.

  Entry Cards

    Title — What this guideline covers (e.g., Brand Voice and Tone).
    Key — Internal identifier (e.g., brand_voice).

  All future AI content generation will use the updated guidelines immediately.

  Where This Context Is Used
  
    Blog post generation — When you click Create Post in Planned Posts, Claude uses these guidelines to write the article.
    AI translations — French and English translations follow the translation rules entry.
    Content suggestions — When Claude suggests image concepts, internal links, or meta descriptions, it uses the brand guidelines.
  

  Quick Tips
  
    Keep guidelines concise but specific. Avoid jargon is vague. Use film souvenir not memory video is actionable.
    Update the target audience entry when your market strategy changes (e.g., expanding to Canadian French market).
    The translation rules entry is critical for maintaining consistent French terminology across all bilingual content.
    If Claude starts generating off-brand content, check the Brand Voice and Tone entry first — it is the most influential guideline.

HelpThis ScreenAI Creator
Generate blog posts using AI, powered by Brand Brain context. The AI writes in MEMOPYK's voice using your brand guidelines.

Step 1: Configure
Fill in the following fields:

  Topic - Describe what the blog post should be about (required)
  Language - French (FR) or English (EN)
  Primary Keyword - The main SEO keyword to target
  Secondary Keywords - Additional keywords (comma-separated)
  Notes - Any special instructions or angles for the AI
  Word Count - Target length (default 900 words)

Click Generate to start. Generation takes 15-30 seconds.

Step 2: Review & Save
The AI generates a complete article with:

  Title, slug, and meta description
  Formatted HTML content with headings, paragraphs, and image placeholders
  SEO metadata and suggested tags

Review the content in the editor, make any adjustments, then click Save Blog Post.

How Brand Brain Works
The AI reads all your Brand Brain entries (brand identity, tone, writing rules, audience, SEO guidelines) to generate content that matches MEMOPYK's voice. Edit Brand Brain in the AI Context tab to improve results.

Tips

  Be specific with your topic for better results
  Always review and edit AI content before publishing
  Use the Blog Editor's AI Assist for quick in-editor generation
  Start with Draft status and review before publishing

HelpThis ScreenKeywords (107)
SEO keywords from Google Keyword Planner, organized for content planning.

Quick Filters
One-click presets for common keyword analysis tasks:

  🎯 Quick Wins — Low competition + High intent keywords in Tier 1-2. Your easiest path to conversions. Start here.
  📈 Traffic Drivers — High-volume Tier 2 keywords (1,000+ searches/mo). Build authority and brand awareness.
  💰 Money Keywords — All high-intent keywords in Tier 1-2, regardless of competition. Your full conversion universe.
  🇫🇷 France Priority — French market Tier 1-2 keywords. Focus on your home market advantage.
  ✍️ Blog Ideas — Medium intent, low-medium competition keywords. Perfect for content calendar planning.
  ✕ Clear — Reset all filters to default.

Click any preset to instantly apply its filters. The preset deactivates if you manually change any filter.

Filtering
Use the dropdowns above each column to filter:

  Search — Type to find specific keywords
  Cluster — Content category (Gift Retirement, VHS Legacy, etc.)
  Market — 🇫🇷 France or 🇺🇸 US
  Tier — Relevance to MEMOPYK service
  Searches/mo — Monthly search volume ranges
  Comp. — How hard to rank (Low/Medium/High)
  Intent — Buyer readiness

Each filter supports multi-select: check/uncheck individual options, use Select All to toggle all. Click OK to apply, Cancel to revert.

Table Columns

  Keyword — The search term. Cluster shown inline as a 🏷️ Gift Retirement tag
  Market — 🇫🇷 FR = France, 🇺🇸 US = United States
  Tier — How relevant to MEMOPYK:
    
      Tier 1 = Direct service match (best!)
      Tier 2 = High relevance
      Tier 3 = Secondary
    
  
  Searches/mo — Monthly search volume from Google
  Competition — How hard to rank:
    
      Low = Easy to rank (good!)
      Medium = Moderate effort
      High = Hard to rank
    
  
  Intent — Conversion likelihood:
    
      High = Ready to buy (best!)
      Medium = Comparing options
      Low = Just researching
    
  
  Planned Posts — Number of planned posts targeting this keyword. Click to view in the Planned Posts tab.
  Posts — Number of published posts using this keyword. Click to view in the Posts tab.


Actions

  ✏️ Edit — Modify keyword details
  🗑️ Delete — Remove (with confirmation)


Best Strategy

  Start with Quick Wins preset — these are your best ROI keywords
  Use Traffic Drivers for brand awareness content
  Create planned posts targeting these keywords first
  Track progress via the Planned Posts and Posts counts
